text:
elaine (pm): Quick sync idea — propose a small pilot for "workload-shaped" pricing profiles. Customers pick either `latency` or `cost` profile and we route/gate to appropriate model variants + routing policy. Want to capture product/contract constraints before we loop in sales.

mike (sales): interesting — helps field asks for lower-cost dev envs. what would the add-on look like? flat fee? credits? :thinking_face: 

elaine (pm): thinking two levers: 1) profile tag on tenant that affects default routing (latency -> higher-cost model/priority lane, cost -> quantized model + aggressive batching). 2) optional "Workload Profile" add-on (monthly) that guarantees a profile assignment + X burst credits.

sam (eng): tech notes: runtime already supports routing by policy and model variant fallback. main infra work is new per-tenant routing key + metrics for QoS. Estimated 3 sprints to be safe, can be trimmed.

rohit (devex): SDK surfaces: a boolean flag in the init + ability to override per-request. docs + quickstart required for launch. We should define sample prompts to validate quality delta.

abby (finance): pricing questions: if it's monthly add-on, need per-tenant price. propose $199/mo for profile + 50k burst tokens? we should model unit economics vs current hosted ARPU.

rowan (pm): launch criteria suggestion: 1) implement routing + UI toggle, 2) sales pilot with 3 customers, 3) quality delta under 5% for key eval sets, 4) contract clause defined.

nina (legal): we need a simple contract clause for profile guarantees and burst handling. Draft: ```If Customer purchases the Workload Profile add-on, Redwood will route eligible inference requests in accordance with the chosen profile. Redwood does not guarantee output parity between profiles. Bursts are subject to capacity and may be throttled; Redwood will provide X burst credits per billing period and notify Customer of sustained usage beyond credits.``` Need to review definitions for "eligible" and "sustained".

kevin (ops): capacity note: for latency profile we should reserve small dedicated pool or priority queue; that impacts SLA and cost. Ops can provision a soft-reserve for pilot but for scale we need committed capacity contracts.

mike (sales): for pilots customers want a trial window. Can we offer free pilot month and then convert? Also, important: can we support regional profile enforcement (EU vs US)? they ask for data residency.

sam (eng): regional routing is doable, but increases infra surface and testing. For pilot, we can scope to US-only; multi-region as phase 2.

abby (finance): if we do soft-reserve, we should price as add-on + optional committed capacity SKU. Two-stage offering: Workload Profile (subscription) + Reserve Pack (committed GPUs) priced separately.

rowan (pm): decision points for next week: - Pilot scope: US-only, 3 customers, 1-month trial - Billing construct: subscription + optional reserve SKU - Launch owner: elaine (PM) - Eng owner: sam - Sales pilot lead: mike - Legal/contract draft: nina - DevEx docs: rohit

elaine (pm): I'll put a short MRD and rollout checklist by EOD Fri. Also attaching the minimal contract text to iterate. Please reply with vetoes (esp. legal/finance/ops).

nina (legal): quick flag — need to add data residency bullet and a clause about change in routing behavior (we should preserve ability to change variant if safety/regulatory concerns). I'll add redlines.

abby (finance): finance OK with pilot economics if we keep reserve optional. will run a sensitivity analysis on $199 + 50k burst. request: model break-even at 5/10/20 pilot signups.

rohit (devex): I'll draft quickstart + sample eval set (latency-sensitive chat + cost-optimized batch) and link it in MRD.

kevin (ops): ops will stand up a soft-reserve pool for the pilot in us-west-2. ETA 2 weeks. Need exact QPS estimate from sales pilots.

mike (sales): I'll recruit 3 pilot customers this week. target: 1 mid-market (SaaS), 2 startups. will ask for usage shaping data.

rowan (pm): no objections from me. If everyone OK, we'll schedule a 30m kickoff Wed to finalize scope. :thumbsup:

elaine (pm): thanks — noted owners. Last ask: anyone who thinks the subscription + reserve split is bad, speak now or we'll proceed.

sam (eng): looks fine from infra side.

nina (legal): will post redlines tomorrow.

abby (finance): will share the sensitivity model by Tue.

rohit (devex): working on docs.

kevin (ops): will confirm pool sizes in kickoff.

mike (sales): hunting customers now.

rowan (pm): OK, locking kickoff Wed 10am PT.
